_comment: Stage 2 alignment hypotheses. Every option is status=concept: drawn by this project from OSM road reserves and trip generators, not from any official or unofficial map. Anchors are resolved against OSM features by name; 'fallback_lonlat' is used only if the name match fails, and the run report says which was used. Routing follows the OSM road graph between anchors, preferring the listed roads (elevated guideways are normally built over road reserves). Vias are kept to termini and true branch points; intermediate centers are forced stations (their offset from the line is reported in run_report.json), so the route is not pulled into neighborhoods.

EDL.label: Point on the Eastern Dispersal Link (E14) viaduct near Jalan Bakar Batu

options.name: Jalan Tebrau spine
options.rationale: Follows Federal Route 3 (Jalan Tebrau, then Jalan Pandan and Jalan Kota Tinggi), the road the official 'Tebrau' name and the congestion claim refer to. Serves the Pelangi/KSL retail cluster and Tebrau City (AEON, IKEA, Toppen), ending at Desa Tebrau. Wide trunk reserve for most of its length.

options.name: FT3 with Taman Molek deviation
options.rationale: Same FT3 spine as T1, but leaves Jalan Pandan to run through Taman Molek (dense residential) on Jalan Persiaran Molek Utama before rejoining at Tebrau City. Tests whether a deviation into a residential core is worth the extra length.

options.name: Jalan Tebrau to Mount Austin
options.rationale: Same FT3 spine as T1 to Tebrau City, then turns west on Jalan Mutiara Emas Utama to end in Mount Austin (high-rise residential and commercial growth area) instead of Desa Tebrau.

options.name: Eastern Dispersal Link (E14) reserve
prefer_roads: Johor Bahru Eastern Dispersal Link Expressway
Lebuhraya Skim Penyuraian Trafik Johor Bahru Timur
options.rationale: Tested because the existing elevated Eastern Dispersal Link (E14) reserve could host a guideway. Rejected if walk catchments and bus interchange are poorer than the FT3 options; metrics are computed so the rejection rests on numbers.

options.name: Larkin - Kangkar Tebrau - Mount Austin
options.rationale: Rejected on scope: Larkin belongs to the Skudai-Tampoi-Larkin corridor (out of scope, owner decision 2). Geometry is computed only to show the rejection; it is not a Skudai option.

options.name: Coastal direct to Puteri Harbour and Kota Iskandar
options.rationale: Shortest reserve from Bukit Chagar to the Iskandar Puteri administrative center, along the coastal roads (J1 and the Iskandar Coastal Highway). Expected to exceed the reported 14.78 km; the deviation itself is a finding.

options.name: Coastal to Perling and Bukit Indah
options.rationale: Ends at Bukit Indah, the largest established residential and retail center in Iskandar Puteri, instead of the administrative core. Tests which endpoint is consistent with the reported 14.78 km.

options.name: Coastal - Bukit Indah - Medini - Kota Iskandar
options.rationale: Serves both Bukit Indah and Kota Iskandar. Longest option; tests the coverage-versus-length trade-off.

options.name: FT1 and coastal highway to Perling and Bukit Indah (shortest reserve)
options.rationale: Follows the shortest road reserve from Bukit Chagar to Bukit Indah: Jalan Tun Abdul Razak (FT1) north-west, then the Iskandar Coastal Highway to Perling and Bukit Indah. Its length matches the reported 14.78 km. Caveat: the first ~6 km on FT1 is the same reserve a future Skudai line would likely use toward Tampoi (Skudai is out of scope, owner decision 2).

rejected_without_geometry.name: Via Skudai Highway (FT1) through Tampoi to Bukit Indah
rejected_without_geometry.reason: Continues on FT1 beyond the coastal-highway junction into Tampoi, which is the Skudai corridor (out of scope, owner decision 2). IP4 uses only the city end of FT1 and turns onto the coastal highway.

rejected_without_geometry.name: Via Second Link Expressway (E3)
rejected_without_geometry.reason: Controlled-access expressway: no frontage, few pedestrian crossings, stations would be unreachable on foot; serves no established center between Perling and Bukit Indah that the coastal options miss.

rejected_without_geometry.name: Any route copied from James Clark's concept map or its Google Map
rejected_without_geometry.reason: Excluded source (SRC-031). Brief forbids copying its geometry.
